job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were watching the news when a debate about a new education policy started. Meera asked, 'Does the Prime Minister decide everything alone?' Rohan shook his head, explaining that while the Prime Minister is the head of the government, the President is the formal head of the country. He pointed out that the political executive, like the Prime Minister and ministers, makes the major policy decisions, while the permanent executive, consisting of civil servants, assists them by providing information and implementing these decisions. Meera then wondered if the Rajya Sabha had the final say on money bills since it is the Upper House. Rohan clarified that in our parliamentary democracy, the Lok Sabha is more powerful because its members are directly elected by the people. If there is a disagreement between the two houses, the Lok Sabha's view usually prevails. Finally, they discussed the judiciary. Rohan emphasized that the Supreme Court remains independent of the legislature and executive, ensuring that laws follow the Constitution. The civil servants do not make the final policy choices; they only execute the plans decided by the elected representatives. This system ensures that the power remains with the people's representatives, keeping the government accountable to the citizens of India.

items.evidence: Rohan shook his head, explaining that while the Prime Minister is the head of the government, the President is the formal head of the country.
items.q: How are the roles of the Prime Minister and the President different?
options: PM heads the government; President formally heads the country
PM heads both the government and the country
President heads the government; PM heads the country
Parliament heads the country; PM heads the government
items.explain: The Prime Minister is head of the government, but the President is the formal head of the country.

wrong.why: thinks the Prime Minister is head of the country
thinks Parliament is the head of the country
